 COMMON JUDGMENT  The petitioner in M.V.C.No.4944/2022 filed claim petition under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident. 
 SCCH-24 3 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022  2. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.4945/2022 filed claim petition under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident. 
 3. These two petitions have arisen out of same accident. Petitioners and respondents are one and the same. Therefore as per order on I.A.No.I, these two petitions have been clubbed together for common evidence and common disposal. 
 4. The case of the petitioners is as follows:-
 That on 05-09-2022 at about 11-15 a.m., the petitioner in M.V.C. No.4944/2022 as pillion rider and petitioner in MVC No 4945/ 2022 as rider was proceeding in a Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-EZ- 7983 near Sarjapura bus stand, Anekal Taluk,
Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Maruthi Alto car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MH-2064 came rashly and negligently without caring for human safety dashed against the aforesaid motorcycle, result of which the petitioners in both the cases have sustained injuries.
 SCCH-24 4 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022  5. Immediately after the accident the petitioner Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
2 in MVC.No.4944/2022 was taken to Spandana Hospital for treatment. The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2, 00,000/- towards hospitalization and other incidental charges etc. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy. She was working as nurse and earning sum of Rs.20, 000/- per month. 
Due to the permanent disability suffered on account of grievous injuries she is not in a position to do the work. She has suffered mental pain and agony,
discomfort and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages. 
 6. Immediately after the accident the petitioner in MVC No. 4945/2022 was taken to Spandana Hospital for treatment. The petitioner has spent more than Rs.2, 00,000/- towards hospitalization and other incidental charges etc. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy. He was working as a marketing executive and earning sum of Rs.20, 000/-
per month. Due to the permanent disability suffered on account of grievous injuries he is not in a position to do the work. He has suffered mental pain and  SCCH-24 5 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 agony, discomfort and other pecuniary and non- pecuniary damages. 
 7. Respondent No.1 /insurer of car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MH-2064 in both the cases has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy. It is contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle who was riding his vehicle without having valid and effective driving license. It is further contended that the driver of offending car was also not having valid and effective driving licence. Hence, respondent no.1 is not liable to pay the compensation. 
 8. In spite of service of summons, the respondent No.2 has remained absent, hence he was placed ex-parte. 
 9. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed in M.V.C.No 4944/2022.
 SCCH-24 6 MVC 4944/2022  c /w Yashvanth .V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
3  4945/2022  ISSUES  1. Whether the petitioner proves that she  had sustained grievous injuries in the  RTA alleged to have occurred on 05-09-  2022 at about 11-15 a.m., near  Sarjapura bus stand, Anekal Taluk,
 Bengaluru District, due to rash and  negligent driving of the driver of Maruti  Alto car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MH-  2064?
 2. Whether the petitioner proves that she  is entitled to the compensation amount  as claimed? if so from whom and to  what extent?
 3. What order or Award?
 10. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed in M.V.C.No.4945/2022. 
 ISSUES  1. Whether the petitioner proves that he  had sustained grievous injuries in the  RTA alleged to have occurred on 05-09-  2022 at about 11-15 a.m., near  Sarjapura bus stand, Anekal Taluk,
 Bengaluru District, due to rash and  negligent driving of the driver of Maruti  Alto car bearing Reg.No.KA-51-MH-  2064?
 SCCH-24 7 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022  2. Whether the petitioner proves that  he is entitled to the compensation  amount as claimed? if so from whom  and to what extent?
 3. What Order or Award? 
 11. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.4944/2022 got examined herself as PW1. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.4945/2022 got examined himself as Pw2 and two witnesses are examined as PW.3 and 4 and got marked Exs.P1 to 15. The respondent No.1 has not adduced any evidence on their behalf. During the cross-examination of PW.1 the learned counsel for Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/ 
4 respondent no.1 has confronted the photographs and got marked it as Ex.R1.
 12. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and learned counsel for respondent no.1.
 13. My findings on the above issues in M.V.C.No.4944/2022 are as follows:-
 Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 - Partly in the affirmative  Issue No. 3- As per final Order.
 for the following :
 SCCH-24 8 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022  14. My findings on the above issues in M.V.C.No.4945/2022 are as follows:-
 Issue No. 1 - In the Affirmative,
 Issue No. 2 - Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No. 3 - As per final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS  15. Issue No.1 and 2 in M.V.C.NO.4944/2022 and M.V.C.No.4945/2022 :- As these issues are interconnected they are taken up together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts. 
 P.W.1- Nirmala Muniyappa is the petitioner in MVC 4944/2022 and P.W.2 - Yashvanth is the petitioner in MVC No.4945/2022. P.W.1 and Pw2 have given evidence to the effect that at the time of accident P.W.1 as pillion rider and Pw.2 as rider in the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-08-EA-7982 were proceeding towards Sarjapura bus stand, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-51-MH-2064(hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came at very high speed, in  SCCH-24 9 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the motorcycle ridden by the P.W.2 and caused the accident, result of which both of them have sustained Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
5 grievous injuries. 
 16 . In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 and PW.2 have relied upon Ex.P1 to P5 and Ex.P8 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, charge sheet,
wound certificate and notice issued u/Sec.133 of IMV act and reply to the said notice. 
 17. On the basis of the complaint lodged by petitioner/Yeshavantha in MVC No.4944/2022, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0230/2022 of Sarjapura Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279,
337 of MV Act. The Investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC. 
 SCCH-24 10 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022  18. On the perusal of the materials it can be gathered that on the basis of the statement as per Ex.P1 given by the PW.2, the FIR was registered against the driver of offending vehicle. If the spot mahazar is perused, the accident in question has occurred on the southern edge of the road. It means,
the spot of accident is on the left side of the road. It is not in dispute that at the time of accident the offending vehicle and motorcycle was proceeding on the same direction towards Sarajapura bus stand. The motorcycle was proceeding ahead of the offending vehicle. The offending vehicle which came from behind the motorcycle hit against the motorcycle on its rear side. Hence, only as per the IMV report at Ex.P3, the front portion of the offending vehicle and rear portion of the motorcycle was damaged. The driver and owner of the offending vehicle have not stepped into the witness box to disprove the case of the petitioners. 
Even the respondent no.1 also has not taken any steps to negative the contention taken by the petitioners. 
Hence, materials placed on record clearly prove the issue no.1. Hence, issue no.1 in MVC No.4944/2022  SCCH-24 11 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 Yashvanth . V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
6 and in MVC No.4945/2022 is answered in the affirmative. 
 19. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4944/2022 :-
P.W.1 has given evidence to the effect of her sustained severe injuries. Petitioner has produced abundant medical documents. As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.5 and Ex.P.6. On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Spandana Hospital, Bangalore from 05-09-2022 to 07- 09-2022 for a period of 3 days. As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained two injuries which are grievous in nature. 
 20. Dr.Chidanand K J C - Orthopedic Surgeon and Professor at Sanjaj Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Bengaluru has given evidence as Pw3 and through him OPD slip and X-ray are got marked as Ex.P.12 and Ex.P13. PW.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 01-02-2024 for assessment of disability. PW.3 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of upper limb at 31% and to the whole body at 10.33%.
 SCCH-24 12 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022  21. Admittedly, PW.3 is not a treated doctor and though PW.3 has denied that petitioner has taken conservative treatment and though PW.3 has stated that Pw.1 has undergone surgery but nowhere has deposed that petitioner requires further treatment. It is deposed by PW.3 that he has not advised the petitioner to take further treatment and that the disability assessed by him is only of physical disability but not functional disability. 
 22. At the cost of repetition, according to the Pw.3 the petitioner has suffered physical disability on whole body at 10.33%. If the documents produced by the respondent no.1 at Ex.R1 and also the evidence of PW.1 are perused, it is admitted fact that at the time of taking the photographs as per Ex.R1 on 14-01-2023,
the petitioner was working in the hospital as a nurse. 
Though PW.1 at the first instance has denied her continued nursing job even after the accident but when Ex.R1 was confronted to her and posed suggestion that Ex.R1 was taken on 14-01-2023 in her working place, the PW.1 admitted the said fact and Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
7 further admitted that she is getting salary equal to that  SCCH-24 13 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 of the salary which she was drawing earlier to the accident. When it is proved that even after the accident petitioner has continued her job and fetching very same salary which she was fetching earlier to the accident, under such circumstances, even if this court considers the percentage of disability assessed by the PW.3, but petitioner will not get compensation under the head loss of future income. For the disability allegedly suffered by the petitioner she may entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomforts but not under the head loss of future income. 
 23. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries. Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/-
towards pain and sufferings. 
 24. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, she has produced medical  SCCH-24 14 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 bills for Rs.64,040/- as per Ex.P.7. In the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to disprove these bills but only suggestions are put about creation of medical bills and the said suggestion has been denied by the Pw1. If the evidence of PW.2 is perused, he has admitted that the owner of the offending vehicle has met sum of Rs.45,000/- towards medical expenses of PW.1 and PW.2. By referring the evidence of PW.2 it is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.1 that the PW.1 and PW.2 are not entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses. 
 25. Per contra, it is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for petitioner that the owner of the offending vehicle has not given any evidence to the effect of the medical expenses to the tune of Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
8 Rs.45,000/- met by him, hence, no amount can be deducted under the head medical expenses. 
 26. When PW.2 who is the injured himself has admitted the fact of medical expenses to the tune of Rs.45,000/- met by the owner of offending vehicle,
 SCCH-24 15 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 there is no need to give evidence to that effect by the owner of the offending vehicle. As per Sec.58 of the Evidence Act "Admitted facts need not be proved" 
Hence, the very admission of the PW.2 itself is sufficient to hold that out of the medical expenses incurred by the PW.1 and PW.2, sum of Rs.45,000/-
was met by the owner of offending vehicle. Hence, out of the medical expenses to the tune of Rs.64,040/-
incurred by the PW.1 sum of Rs.22,500/- is to be deducted. As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.41,540/- under the head medical expenses. 
 27. It is stated that petitioner was working as a nurse and earning sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. To substantiate the said contention, the petitioner has not produced any materials. Hence considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of petitioner this court considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
 28. The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 3 days as an inpatient in Spandana Hospital, Bengaluru. Hence the nature of  SCCH-24 16 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 injury sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature, it is reasonable to hold that period of two months as complete laid down period. Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.15,500/- p.m for two months. Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.31,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period. 
 29. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
9 medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Spandana Hospital, Bengaluru. Further for 3 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment. She has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses. Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.15,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022.
 30. It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident the petitioner was aged about 24 years. The  SCCH-24 17 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 petitioner has not produced any authenticated documents to prove her age. In medical records, the age of petitioner is shown as 24 years. Hence considering the medical records and petition this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 24 years. 
 31 . The petitioner at her age of 24 years has suffered two grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life. Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.1,25,000/- towards loss of comfort and amenities. 
Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl.N Heads Amount Rs.
o.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.60,000/-
 2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 15,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 31,000/-
 laid up period  4. Medical expenses Rs. 41,540/-
 5. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.1,25,000/-
 Total Rs.2,72,540/-
 SCCH-24 18 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,72,540/- (Rupees Two Lakh Seventy Two Thousand Five Hundred Forty only).
 32. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.4945/2022- P.W.2 Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
10 has given evidence to the effect of his sustained severe injuries. Petitioner has produced abundant medical documents. As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents which are at Ex.P.9 and Ex.P.10 On going through the medical documents; it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment at Spandana Hospital, Bangalore from 05-09-2022 to 10- 09-2022 for a period of 4 days. As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained three injuries which are grievous in nature. 
 33. Dr.Chidanand K J C - Orthopedic Surgeon and Professor Orthopedics at Sanjaj Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Bengaluru has given evidence as Pw4 and through him OPD slip and X-ray are got marked as Ex.P.14 and Ex.P15. PW.4 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 01-02- 2024 for assessment of disability. PW.4 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent  SCCH-24 19 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 physical disability of upper limb at 30% and to the whole body at 10.00%. PW.4 further deposed that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants at an approximate cost of Rs.20,000/-. 
 34. If the cross examination of PW.4 is carefully perused, admittedly he is not a treated doctor and except discharge summary he has not verified any of the medical records for the treatment taken by the petitioner. As per the own evidence of Pw4 the clavicle fracture of the petitioner is united and since petitioner is person of young age all the injuries are healed within six weeks and since he has assessed the disability of the petitioner after lapse of three years from the date of accident by that time the injuries suffered by the petitioner was healed and that he has assessed only the physical disability but not the functional disability of the petitioner . 
 35. In the light of the evidence given by the PW.4 if the evidence of PW.2 is perused, though PW.2 has deposed that earlier to the accident he was working as Marketing Executive and due to the accident he is unable to work etc but no document has been  SCCH-24 20 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
11 produced either to prove that he was working as Managing Executive or to prove that due to the accidental injuries suffered by him he has quite the job or that he was removed from the job. Hence, this court declines to award compensation under the head loss of future income due to the physical disability. From the alleged percentage of disability it would have caused some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort to the petitioner hence he is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.1,25,000/-. 
 36. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained three grievous injuries. Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.60,000/-
towards pain and sufferings. 
 37 . So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are concerned, he has produced medical bills for Rs.1,38,791/- as per Ex.P.11. Out of which for the  SCCH-24 21 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 reason stated supra while answering Issue no.2 in MVC No.4944/2022, sum of Rs.22,500/- has to be deducted. Under such circumstances, PW.2 is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,16,291/-. 
 38 . It is stated that petitioner was working as a marketing executive and earning sum of Rs.20,000/-
per month. To substantiate the said contention,
petitioner has not produced any materials. Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence of petitioner considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
 39. The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and has taken treatment for 4 days as an inpatient in Spandana Hospital, Bengaluru. Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature, it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period. Hence taking in to consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this court Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
12 takes the loss of income during the laid down period as  SCCH-24 22 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 Rs.15,500/- p.m for two months. Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.31,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
 40. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Spandana Hospital, Bengaluru. Further for 4 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment. He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses. Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022. 
 41. As per the evidence of Pw4, the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant the estimated cost of the surgery is Rs.20,000/-. But admittedly PW.4 has not given estimation. Hence, this court inclines to award future medical expenses only to the tune of Rs.15,000/-. Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
 SCCH-24 23 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 Sl.N Heads Amount Rs.
o.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs.60,000/-
 2 . Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs.20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  3. Towards loss of income during Rs.31,000/-
 laid up period  4. Medical expenses Rs.1,16,291/-
 5. Future medical expenses Rs.15,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities and Rs.1,25,000/-
 discomfort 7. Total Rs.3,67,291/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,67,291/- (Rupees Three Lakh Sixty Seven Thousand Two Hundred Ninety One only).
Yashvanth . V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
13  42. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 1 st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident. Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle. Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident. Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 1 this court directs the respondent no.1  SCCH-24 24 MVC 4944/2022  c /w  4945/2022 to pay compensation to the both petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount. Hence, I answers Issue no 2 in partly affirmative. 
 43. Issue No.3 in MVC No.4944/2022 and M.V.C.No.4945/2022 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2 in MVC No.4944/2022 and MVC No.4945/2022, finding on this issue is as per the following final order. 
 ORDER The claim petitions filed by the petitioner in MVC No. 4944/2022 and MVC No. 4945/2022 are hereby allowed in part with costs. 
The petitioner in M.V.C.No.4944/2022 is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,72,540/- (Rupees Two Lakh Seventy Two Thousand Five Hundred Forty only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit. 
c /w 4945/2022 The petitioner in MVC No.4945/2022 is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,67,291/- (Rupees Three Lakh Sixty Seven Thousand Two Hundred Ninety one only) with interest at 6% per annum on Rs.3,52,291/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit. 
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest at 6% p.a. Within 2 months from the date of award. 
On deposit of the said amount, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner in M.V.C.No.
4944/2022, shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification. 
c /w 4945/2022 On deposit of the said amount, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner in M.V.C.No. 4945/2022, shall be deposited in the name of petitioner in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner Yashvanth.V vs National Ins Co Ltd on 4 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107970935/
14 through E-payment on proper identification. 
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- each in MVC No. 4944/2022 and 4945/2022. 
Keep the original Judgment in MVC No.4944/2022 and the copy in MVC No.4945/2022. 
Draw award accordingly.
